## Islamic Philosophy quotes

Islamic philosophy names the classical falsafa tradition and related theological-philosophical debate across the Islamic world.

36 passages · 6 voices in this archive selection

### Overview

Figures such as al-Farabi, Avicenna (Ibn Sina), Averroes (Ibn Rushd), and al-Ghazali debate intellect, prophecy, causation, and the relation of philosophy to revelation. The archive gathers English renderings with honest confidence marks when Arabic originals are not transcribed.

### Historical notes

From the translation movement through Andalusian Aristotelianism and later critiques, Islamic philosophy shaped Jewish and Latin scholastic thought as well as its own lineages.

### Core ideas

-   Philosophy and prophecy can be ordered without collapsing into each other.
-   Metaphysics of being and intellect remains central (especially Avicenna).
-   Demonstrative science has norms that rhetoric and dialectic do not replace.
-   Critique of the philosophers is itself a philosophical act (al-Ghazali and responses).

### FAQ

#### What is Islamic philosophy?

It is the philosophical tradition developed in Islamic civilizations, often engaging Greek sources alongside Qur’anic and legal discourse.

#### Who are key Islamic philosophers?

Common entry points include al-Farabi, Avicenna, Averroes, al-Ghazali, Ibn Tufayl, and Ibn Khaldun.
